title: After last update, podman-desktop consumes a lot of CPU and memory when idle
body:
### Bug description

Hello, 
I've updated my podman and podman-desktop install on my Windows machine and now I have `podman-desktop` process taking consistently 20 to 30% of the CPU and up to 4GB of memory, while doing nothing (I have no images, container or anything being used). 

Is this expected?

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e8f130c4-d20e-4e43-b929-504952a8ecab)


### Operating system

Microsoft Windows 11 [Version 10.0.22635.4580]

### Installation Method

Scoop (Windows)

### Version

1.14.2

### Steps to reproduce

Just run `podman-desktop`, and after a while it starts taking much memory. The UI becomes almost irresponsive, very sluggish. And the fans of my PC start running full speed. 

### Relevant log output

```shell

```

### Additional context

_No response_

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: @reporter It is not expected. You have no images or container running, but do you have podman VM running?

comments.author: reporter
comments.body: @participant1 Yes!

comments.body:
@reporter is it running with Hyper-V or WSL?

My podman desktop is running on Windows 10 for about 5H and I don't see any increase in memory consumption or sluggish UI yet.

Do you have anything else running, like kind cluster, Docker, OpenShift Local?
Do you have current context in kubeconfig pointing to active kubernetes cluster?

Anything that helps to replicate the issue are greatly appreciated. Thanks!

I've started it again, and tracked using Process Monitor for a while. It indeed kept growing in memory and CPU usage from the 300M you mention up to ~1G, when I stopped tracking.

It seems to be spending most of the time reading `app.asar`. Whatever that is.

Have you tried to restart podman? Has it helped?

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: I can replicate CPU load in case of podman connections issues, but it does not lead to memory leak and sluggish UI.

comments.author: participant2
comments.body: Is this caused by #8681?

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: Unstable connection can be the cause. PD is trying to reconnect in 5 seconds and creates new Dockerode instance for that. In come cases new Dockerode instances are not garbage collected. That can lead to both CPU load and memory consumption.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
> I can replicate CPU load in case of podman connections issues, but it does not lead to memory leak and sluggish UI.

@participant1 it really needs quite an amount of time to pile up the memory...

comments.author: reporter
comments.body: And for me it replicates systematically. Also after a restart of Podman Desktop or WSL2 or the machine itself: After 30min - 1h I have the cpu at ~30% and memory at 1GB and increasing.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: My previous manager gave me an idea how to replicate that. I will try to ssh to podman vm and try to simulate slowness one way or another and then we figure out how to avoid memory leak over time.

how many CPU/memory is being used by the podman machine itself ?

`podman machine ssh top -b -n 1`
`podman machine ssh free -h`


do you have a firewall that could impact the connection to the ports of the machine (based on the log file it seems Podman Desktop is not able to communicate with the machine but the machine is reporting it's alive so it's like doing infinite reconnection)
